entries.gave: Read the Cut, its decisions and the one More kept (code N8: a quotation mark that never closes ends in a _csv.Error traceback in a long file, and hides the mark in a short one), and invoicer as it stands: command.py, lines.py, render.py, totals.py, tax.py, pyproject.toml, .gitignore and the tests. Its people are the accounting colleagues, who run `invoicer LINES --rate PERCENT` on a file saved from their spreadsheet and get the invoice printed, or one line saying what to fix, and the developers and code that use the package. lines.py reads with csv.reader, which raises _csv.Error for an unclosed quote in a long file and, in a short one, reads the rest of the file into one cell, so the refusal names a later fault or none.
Read code best-practice.md with template.md, and refactor-code best-practice.md, to their end before any change.

Decided: take the Cut decision "a wrong line" as it stands; in lines.py read rows by csv.reader with strict=True, through one generator _rows that numbers rows as the spreadsheet does and turns csv.Error into LineError naming the row where the quoted cell opens, with a message to remove the mark or close the cell. Settled by the purpose: a cell with text after its closing mark, such as "Pro" x, is refused by the same message, as it reads in no one way and a spreadsheet never saves it. No asks.

Specification: the Cut decision "a wrong line" and the More kept; unit cases added: test_refuses_a_quotation_mark_that_never_closes_naming_the_row_where_it_opens (command), and in lines test_refuses_a_quotation_mark_that_never_closes_naming_the_row_where_it_opens, test_refuses_a_quotation_mark_that_never_closes_in_a_long_file, test_refuses_a_cell_with_text_after_its_closing_quotation_mark.
Left to the code: how an unclosed mark is found (csv strict mode, not a scan of its own, so the quoting rule stays in csv) and the message wording.
The decision goes to invoicer/lines.py, which decides which rows of text give a line; no module added.
No variants called for; none made.
Offered names unchanged (Line, LineError, parse_lines, ROW); the new row reader is internal, _rows.
Planned one branch, the csv.Error catch in _rows, called for by the three new lines cases; no option or parameter added.

Lines cases designed before the code, each supporting the command case test_refuses_a_quotation_mark_that_never_closes_naming_the_row_where_it_opens: a short file (Given row 2 opens "Pro and never closes, Then LineError row 2), a long file (Given 30000 rows after it, Then the same LineError, no csv.Error), text after the closing mark (Given "Pro" x, Then LineError row 2).
Every new case supports a unit case of the command; none to take back.
Inputs from outside: the command line (LINES, --rate) at command.main, the saved file at command.main and its text at parse_lines, where csv first reads it.

Rules searched: the separator (_SEPARATOR, only in lines.py), the reading of quoted cells (csv.reader, once in lines.py), the row numbering from 1 (once, moved into _rows).

Kinds of thing done in many places: refusing a row (LineError with "row N: ..." in lines.py), refusing the command line (parser.error in command.py). The new refusal takes the LineError way with the row prefix.

Each new test passes text and asserts a LineError message or a description, both of which the parse_lines docstring states.
